newsitem.title: USA: Dayton above plan in all divisions for Jan.
newsitem.headline: Dayton above plan in all divisions for Jan.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said January sales were above plan in all divisions, with same-store sales up 5.5 percent overall for the four weeks ended February 1, 1997, compared with the four weeks ended January 27, 1996.
"Our January sales results were above plan at each of our divisions," said chief executive Bob Ulrich.
Here's how Dayton Hudson's January and year-to-date sales fared by operating division:

-- Target's total sales for the month increased 15.2 percent and comparable-store sales increased 6.7 percent. Year-to-date, Target's total sales increased 14.6 percent and comparable-store sales rose 5.8 percent.

-- Mervyn's total sales for the month increased 1.7 percent and comparable-store sales increased 0.4 percent. Year-to-date, Mervyn's total sales declined 2.4 percent and comparable-store sales decreased 4.1 percent.

-- The Department Store Division's total sales for the month increased 7.8 percent and comparable-store sales increased 4.1 percent. Year-to-date, the division's total sales dipped 0.9 percent and comparable-store sales decreased 4.5 percent.

Total company sales for the 52 weeks ended February 1, 1997 were $24.885 billion, up 9.3 percent from $22.763 billion in the same period a year ago. Comparable-store sales for the 52-week period were up 2.5 percent compared to the same period last year.
Dayton Hudson operates large-store general merchandise formats, including discount stores, moderate-priced promotional and traditional department stores. It operates 1,101 stores in 38 states.
